Simplify radiology reporting with variable fields in Eden PACS
Variable Fields let radiologists insert and complete customizable fields within Eden PACS report templates, reducing manual editing while keeping a consistent reporting structure.
Greater visibility into deleted and merged studies in Eden Intelligence
Eden Intelligence now offers a detailed breakdown of deleted and merged studies, helping institutions reconcile uploaded study volumes with billing records.
When the worklist empties, the Garden of Eden opens
New in Eden PACS: when you sign your last study, your screen opens onto a landscape that follows your local time and weather.
Oblique MPR in the main viewer (not only on the MPR viewer)
Standard orthogonal views depend on the scanner's acquisition geometry rather than the patient's actual anatomy. If a patient is misaligned (e.g., tilted head or rotated spine), standard views are effectively oblique. Oblique MPR lets radiologists adjust the reconstruction plane in real time to align with the true anatomy. This feature was available in the MPR viewer; now it is available in the main 2D viewer as well.
Cross-window Drag and Drop
This feature was built to make multi-monitor and side-by-side reading more efficient for radiologists. A single drag-and-drop action replaces the tedious process of finding and reloading a series in a second window.
Quick Actions: Report Refinement and Impression Generation
Report Refinement was introduced to automatically improve grammar, terminology, punctuation, clarity, and readability across radiology reports, while Impression Generation creates concise, prioritized Impression or Conclusion sections directly from documented findings.
Remove Image Obstructions with 3D Clipping
3D Clipping is an interactive editing tool within the volume rendering environment that allows the radiologist to clip selected portions of the 3D study.
Highlight Critical Findings with the New Frontier in Mammography
As part of the improvements aimed at strengthening diagnostic capability in mammography studies, the viewer now incorporates three new post-processing filters: Density, Edges, and Micro-detail, available for the targeted re-evaluation of FFDM and DBT studies. These tools expand the radiologist's ability to interrogate borderline or equivocal findings without leaving the workstation's standard view.
Superior Control, Agile Reading: New Features in the PET-CT Fusion Viewer
In PET-CT, image interpretation depends not only on the quality of the study but also on how efficiently the specialist interacts with the fused anatomical and metabolic information. The new features in our viewer have been designed to give nuclear medicine physicians more direct, precise, and flexible control over how PET findings are displayed on CT images.
